title: Ticket and Email Triage
summary: Classify and route incoming emails, web complaints and tickets by issue, account, urgency and regulatory risk, extract what the resolver needs and draft a first reply for approval.

seo.title: AI Ticket and Email Triage for Telecom | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that classifies emails, web complaints and tickets, reads attachments, flags regulatory escalations, routes to the right queue and drafts replies.

designed_for: Head of Customer Care Back Office

problem.intro: Written complaints arrive by email, web form, app and social media, and as escalations through the nodal officer or appellate channel, in English, Hindi and regional languages, often with bill screenshots or speed-test images attached. First-level agents read each one to decide the category, find the account and route it, and urgent items such as a regulatory escalation, a legal notice or an enterprise link outage wait in the same queue as everything else.

pain_points.title: Manual reading and categorisation
pain_points.detail: Agents read every message to pick a category, and miscategorised tickets bounce between teams.

pain_points.title: Urgency is buried
pain_points.detail: Escalations that mention a regulator, a consumer forum or a legal notice are not visible until someone opens them.

pain_points.title: Missing details
pain_points.detail: The mobile or account number sits in a screenshot or signature, so agents reply asking for information the customer already sent.

pain_points.title: Duplicates across channels
pain_points.detail: The same customer writes by email, web form and social media, creating parallel tickets that different agents work on.

solution.overview: We build a triage service that reads each incoming email, form submission or ticket along with its attachments and prepares it for the resolver. It identifies the language, classifies the issue against your category tree, extracts the mobile or account number, circle, dates, amounts and disputed charges from the text and screenshots, and looks up the customer in the CRM. It assigns priority from your rules, raising anything that mentions a regulator, consumer forum, legal notice or enterprise outage, and links duplicates from the same customer. The ticket lands in the right queue with a summary and a drafted reply in the customer's language, for an agent to approve.
capabilities: Language detection and classification against your category and sub-category tree
Extraction of mobile number, account ID, circle, dates and disputed amounts from text and attachments
OCR for bill screenshots, speed-test images and scanned letters
Priority rules for regulatory escalations, legal notices, repeat complaints and enterprise outages
Duplicate and thread linking across email, web, app and social channels
Drafted replies in the customer's language for agent approval

workflow.title: Receive the message
workflow.detail: Emails, form submissions, app complaints and social tickets arrive in one intake.

workflow.title: Read text and attachments
workflow.detail: The language is detected and attachments such as screenshots and letters are read with OCR.

workflow.title: Classify and extract
workflow.detail: The issue is classified, key fields are extracted and the customer is found in the CRM.

workflow.title: Prioritise and link
workflow.detail: Priority rules run, regulatory and legal mentions are raised, and duplicates are linked.

workflow.title: Confirm uncertain categories
workflow.detail: Low-confidence classifications go to a triage agent before routing.

workflow.title: Route and draft
workflow.detail: The ticket reaches the right queue with a summary and a drafted reply, which the resolver approves and sends.

inputs: Attachments such as bills, screenshots and letters
outputs: Draft replies in the customer's language
human_in_the_loop: Triage agents confirm low-confidence classifications, and resolvers approve every reply before it reaches the customer. Regulatory and legal escalations always go to the named complaints or legal owner and are never answered automatically.
integrations: Ticketing such as Salesforce Service Cloud, Zendesk, Freshdesk, ServiceNow or an in-house CRM
guardrails: No reply sent without agent approval
Regulatory, consumer forum and legal mentions always escalated to a named owner
Draft replies limited to approved templates and knowledge
Confidence thresholds per category, reviewed monthly
compliance_notes: Supports the complaint registration and escalation flow operators run under TRAI's complaint redressal regulations; docket handling stays in your ticketing system.
Customer emails and attachments are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: One inbound mailbox or web complaint queue, evaluated first on historic tickets and then in shadow mode on live traffic.
deliverables: Category tree and priority rules configured
Triage service integrated with your ticketing system in shadow mode
Reply drafts for the top categories
Accuracy report against agents' final categories

what_we_measure.how: System categories compared with the final category agents assigned.
Tickets reassigned after routing, compared with the current process.
Elapsed time from arrival to first reply, from ticketing data.
Regulatory and legal mentions caught on a labelled test set of historic tickets.

faqs.q: Does it handle Hindi and regional-language emails?
faqs.a: Yes. It detects the language, classifies the complaint and drafts the reply in the same language, with an English summary for resolvers who need one.

faqs.q: Will it reply to customers automatically?
faqs.a: Not by default. Drafts go to agents for approval. Some acknowledgement messages can be automated later if you choose, but regulatory and legal escalations are always handled by people.

faqs.q: Does it work with our ticketing system?
faqs.a: Yes, through APIs or webhooks for common platforms such as Salesforce Service Cloud, Zendesk, Freshdesk and ServiceNow, or through your in-house CRM's integration layer.

faqs.q: Can it read screenshots and scanned letters?
faqs.a: Yes. Bill screenshots, speed-test images and scanned letters are read with OCR, and extracted values such as amounts or dates are shown with the image region they came from.
